title: 027 · Why? #15: why a circle's area is πr² (3D rings unroll into a triangle; predict-first)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Area. Unroll each ring of a circle and stack them. What shape do they make? A rectangle · B triangle · C semicircle 👇

B, a triangle. You learned area = πr². Here's why.
Each ring keeps its length when it's straightened. The rim is the longest (2πr), and the rings shrink to nothing at the centre, so they stack into a triangle: base 2πr, height r.
Area = ½ × 2πr × r = πr².
Trap: "a rectangle" (A). That needs every strip the same length, but the inner rings are shorter, so the triangle fills exactly half of the 2πr × r rectangle. (Cutting a circle into slices makes a rough rectangle. Cutting it into rings makes a triangle.)
Adding up thin rings is integration: ∫₀ʳ 2πx dx = πr².

NDA asked about this in 2019 (I), Q76: f(r) = perimeter ÷ area of a circle of radius r. f(1) + f(2) = ? Perimeter ÷ area = 2πr ÷ πr² = 2/r, so 2 + 1 = 3 → (c).
